title: 12TET pitch class closure
statement: Only under explicit twelve-tone equal temperament, pc(x+12n)=pc(x).

title: Equal temperament semitone
statement: Ratio between consecutive 12-TET semitone steps is 2^(1/12).

title: Major triad
statement: A root-position major triad has pitch classes {0,4,7} relative to root in 12-TET.

title: Minor triad
statement: A root-position minor triad has pitch classes {0,3,7} relative to root in 12-TET.

title: Diminished triad
statement: A root-position diminished triad has pitch classes {0,3,6} relative to root.

title: Augmented triad
statement: A root-position augmented triad has pitch classes {0,4,8} relative to root.
scope_limit: Symmetry can yield competing root interpretations.

title: Dominant seventh pitch model
statement: A conventional dominant-seventh chord has relative pitch classes {0,4,7,10}.
scope_limit: A dom7 voicing may omit fifth.

title: Major seventh pitch model
statement: A major-seventh chord has relative pitch classes {0,4,7,11}.

title: Minor seventh pitch model
statement: A minor-seventh chord has relative pitch classes {0,3,7,10}.

title: Half-diminished seventh
statement: A half-diminished seventh chord has relative pitch classes {0,3,6,10}.
scope_limit: May be iiø7 in a minor key.

title: Fully diminished seventh
statement: A fully diminished seventh chord has relative pitch classes {0,3,6,9}.
scope_limit: Written diminished seventh, not major sixth.

title: German H/B conversion
statement: In conventional German note names H corresponds to English B and German B to English Bb.
scope_limit: Not all alphabets treat letters identically.

title: Roman key dependency
statement: Scale-degree interpretation requires a local key/mode or explicitly unknown tonal context.
original_example: Dm=ii in C, iv in A minor
scope_limit: Identical pitches can have multiple analyses.

title: Chord slash-bass
statement: In lead-sheet chord slash notation, suffix after slash denotes specified bass pitch.

title: Transposition class invariant
statement: Under transposition by k semitones, interval classes between pitch classes remain invariant.

title: Modal interval model Dorian
statement: Dorian scale pattern in semitones relative tonic: 0,2,3,5,7,9,10.
original_example: D E F G A B C
scope_limit: Context/tonic cannot be inferred from collection alone.

title: Modal interval model Lydian
statement: Lydian scale pattern: 0,2,4,6,7,9,11.
original_example: F G A B C D E
scope_limit: Major-mode tonic ambiguous from notes alone.

title: Modal interval model Mixolydian
statement: Mixolydian scale pattern: 0,2,4,5,7,9,10.
original_example: G A B C D E F

title: Harmonic minor interval model
statement: Harmonic minor scale intervals: 0,2,3,5,7,8,11.
original_example: A B C D E F G#

title: Whole tone symmetric collection
statement: Whole-tone collection 0,2,4,6,8,10 contains six tones.
original_example: C D E F# G# A#

title: Tn transposition
statement: Tn maps pc p to (p+n) mod 12.

title: TnI inversion
statement: TnI maps pc p to (n-p) mod 12.

title: Parallel P transformation
statement: Neo-Riemannian P switches major/minor while retaining root and fifth.

title: Relative R transformation
statement: Neo-Riemannian R switches to relative triad with two shared notes.
scope_limit: Triadic context; tonal-center not necessarily switched.

title: Leittonwechsel L transformation
statement: Neo-Riemannian L changes one note by semitone to third-related triad.

title: Add9 vs ninth
statement: Cadd9 contains no implied seventh, C9 generally implies minor seventh.
original_example: Cadd9 C E G D; C9 C E G Bb D
scope_limit: Conventions vary in real chord charts.

title: Classical leading tone
statement: Leading tone typically resolves upward by semitone in common-practice cadential context.
scope_limit: Other voices, frustr. resolution and non-classical styles.

title: Dominant seventh tritone
statement: In classical cadences, 7th of V7 often resolves downward by step and leading tone upward.

title: Classical V–I
statement: Dominant harmony conventionally creates potential for tonic closure with suitable placement.
scope_limit: Cadence is a contextual formal function.

title: Predominant to dominant
statement: ii/IV frequently support movement toward V in common-practice syntax.
scope_limit: IV may also close rock songs.

title: Applied dominant target
statement: V7/x tends to tonicize its target x, but need not resolve literally.
scope_limit: Interrupted, deceptive or chained dominant cases.

title: Minor-mode leading tone
statement: V7 in tonal minor often contains raised leading tone.
scope_limit: Aeolian modal practice may prefer v.

title: Classical cadential 64
statement: Cadential I64 is often dominant elaboration rather than independent tonic arrival.

title: Jazz ii–V guide tones
statement: Sevenths and thirds of ii/V frequently resolve by semitone or common tones.

title: Minor iv color
statement: Borrowed minor iv often supports tonic approach in major-key styles.
scope_limit: May be interpreted as mixture or chromatic voice-leading.

title: Chromatic predominant augmented sixth
statement: Aug6 span commonly expands to dominant scale degree 5 in common-practice tonal context.

title: Circle motion
statement: Descending fifth roots are frequent in some tonal and jazz sequences.
scope_limit: Not necessarily normative in modal, rock or gamelan.

title: Blues dominant seventh tonic
statement: I7 often functions tonically in blues-derived repertoires.
original_example: C7 as bar1 in C blues
scope_limit: Do not force every I7 into V/IV.

title: Modal center stability
statement: Modal vamp can establish center through bass, duration, melody without V–I.
scope_limit: Tonic inference uncertain without musical evidence.

title: Popular loop closure
statement: Repeated pop loop may have rhetorical closure at rotation boundary independent of cadential V–I.

title: Cadence strength context
statement: A larger formal closure requires more than a chord-pair identity.

title: Melody-harmony compatibility
statement: Strong melody notes are often chord tones or contextually managed tensions.
scope_limit: Non-chord tones can be compositionally valid.

title: Strong-beat harmonic rhythm
statement: New harmonies often coincide with metrically salient positions in some idioms.

title: Voice leading common tones
statement: Holding common tones can reduce motion cost under fixed matching.

title: Tritone substitution of V7
statement: Replace dominant seventh with tritone-related seventh directed to same goal.
scope_limit: Jazz idiom; voice-leading and spelling review.

title: Relative triad substitution
statement: Move triad to relative mode preserving two notes.

title: Parallel mode switch
statement: Switch major/minor third of chord with same root/fifth.

title: Inversion change
statement: Change bass to chord tone without changing chord's pitch-class set.

title: Voicing redistribution
statement: Revoice same chord tones across register while preserving harmony label.
scope_limit: Doubled notes or omitted fifth may affect sound.

title: Motivic rhythmic augmentation
statement: Multiply note durations by positive constant without changing order.

title: Motivic rhythmic diminution
statement: Divide durations by constant.

title: Melodic retrograde
statement: Reverse pitch event order, with rhythm handling explicit.
scope_limit: Not full retrograde if durations unchanged.

title: Melodic inversion
statement: Invert directed melodic intervals around specified axis.

title: Motivic sequence
statement: Repeat melodic/rhythmic shape at shifted pitch level.

title: Borrowed chord insertion
statement: Replace selected diatonic chord with parallel-mode-derived chord.
scope_limit: Can clash with melody pitch A over Fm.

title: Applied dominant insertion
statement: Precede target with dominant of that target.
scope_limit: Chord durations and voice leading need replanning.

title: Reharmonize fixed melody
statement: Hold melody notes and seek alternative harmony retaining explicit tension policy.
original_example: E melody over Cmaj7 / Am9 / Fmaj7
scope_limit: Need temporal alignment to avoid false compatibility.

title: Arrangement recast
statement: Preserve essential pitch/harmonic plan while reallocating voices to instruments.

title: Roman numeral lens
statement: Interpret pitches relative to selected key/mode and local tonicization.
original_example: Am=vi in C, i in A minor

title: Functional lens
statement: Classify context as tonic/predominant/dominant roles.
original_example: G7 in C has dominant behavior

title: Modal lens
statement: Identify characteristic mode and supporting degrees.

title: Pop multi-tonic lens
statement: Allow relative major/minor focus to coexist.

title: Neo-Riemannian triadic lens
statement: Describe triad changes with P/L/R relationships where defined.
scope_limit: Not a full tonal function theory.

title: Chromatic mediant lens
statement: Describe non-diatonic third-related sonorities and voice-leading.
scope_limit: Historical labels don't yield universal function.

title: Blues-specific function
statement: Treat dominant quality on I/IV as tonic/subdominant in relevant repertoire.

title: Six-based minor notation
statement: Represent relative-minor tonic as scale degree vi under declared pop notation convention.
scope_limit: Not necessarily the actual tonal center.

title: Voice leading displacement
statement: Rank voiced chords by total semitone motion under explicit matching rules.

title: Melody chord-tone preference
statement: Prefer candidates containing emphasized melody tones when requested.

title: Style-conditional recommendation
statement: Filter chord candidates by selected analysis lens and style.
scope_limit: Style labels cannot guarantee a unique grammar.

title: Complexity ladder
statement: Provide conservative, colored, advanced and exploratory variants.

title: Composition contour preservation
statement: When developing motif, preserve selected invariant (contour/rhythm/interval).
scope_limit: Other qualities may be intentionally transformed.

title: Formal contrast budget
statement: Vary one or more of register/texture/harmony/motif to differentiate sections.
scope_limit: No fixed formula guarantees listener perception.

title: Corpus dependence of chord frequency
statement: A chord transition rate has meaning only relative to a named corpus, style, counting grain and sample.
original_example: I–V share varies by rock/classical corpus

title: Tonal ambiguity in axis loops
statement: Published pop research identifies multiple tonal readings of common axis rotations.

title: Plateau loop / hybrid tonic
statement: Research documents pop loops where IV/V/vi and melodic tonic evidence need nuanced analysis.

title: Music expectation is learned
statement: Perceived tension and expectation depend on learned schemas and context.

title: Genre labels are heterogenous
statement: A 'jazz' or 'popular' pattern label does not uniquely identify a harmonic rule set.

title: 12TET MIDI-Klasse
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Nicht auf 19-TET als gleicher Tonklassenbegriff übertragen.

title: Oktave in Standard-MIDI
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Register und Klangfarbe bleiben verschieden.

title: Durleiter-Intervallstruktur
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Chromatik allein genügt nicht für enharmonische Schreibweise.

title: Natürlich-Moll-Struktur
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Harmonisch-Moll verändert die siebte Stufe.

title: Dorisches Profil
non_applicability_or_counterexample: D als Zentrum nicht automatisch aus Menge bestimmbar.

title: Phrygisches Profil
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Tonzentrum muss melodisch bestätigt sein.

title: Lydisches Profil
non_applicability_or_counterexample: F# darf nicht blind als b5 identifiziert werden.

title: Mixolydisches Profil
non_applicability_or_counterexample: F ist b7 und keine diatonische Leitton-F#.

title: Notenname in F#-Dur
non_applicability_or_counterexample: F als Tonklassenersatz verhindert diatonische E-Stufe.

title: Übermäßige Quarte
non_applicability_or_counterexample: C–Gb ist notiert d5.

title: Verminderte Quinte
non_applicability_or_counterexample: C–F# ist notiert A4.

title: Cmaj7 Bestand
non_applicability_or_counterexample: C7 hat Bb statt B.

title: C7 Bestand
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Dominantseptakkord ohne Tonartfunktion.

title: Cadd9 Bestand
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Cmaj9 hat zusätzlich B.

title: G7 Bestand
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Akkord allein legt Tonikaregion nicht fest.

title: Dm7 Bestand
non_applicability_or_counterexample: D-moll-Dreiklang enthält kein C.

title: Am7 Bestand
non_applicability_or_counterexample: A7 hat C# statt C.

title: F#m7 Bestand
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Doppelte Vorzeichen anderer Tonarten brauchen eigenen Speller.

title: Half-diminished Bm7b5
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Bdim7 enthält Ab statt A in dieser Schreibung.

title: Taktlänge 4/4
assertion_or_proposal: Summe der Ereignisdauern pro Stimme/Takt ≤4 mit vollständigem Stimmenrhythmus =4
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Sustains können Taktgrenzen überschreiten, falls explizit notiert.

title: MIDI Tonhöhenbereich
non_applicability_or_counterexample: MIDI2 kann andere Expressivität transportieren, nicht neue hier erfundene Zahl.

title: MIDI Velocity 7bit
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Velocity 0 in NoteOn wird häufig als NoteOff behandelt.

title: Transponieren um Oktave
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Register und Instrumentengrenzen ändern sich.

title: Dauer und Start
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Auftakte können relativ zu taktbezogenem Nullpunkt modelliert werden.

title: Source ID eindeutig
assertion_or_proposal: Jede ID kommt nur einmal vor
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Editionen dürfen eigene IDs bekommen.

title: Theory claim provenance
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Quellenfamilienlink allein ist keine überprüfte Seite.

title: License reuse gate
assertion_or_proposal: Ohne erlaubte Redistribution keine Originalkopien öffentlich übernehmen
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Forschung darf bibliografisch zitieren.

title: Roman numeral contextual key
assertion_or_proposal: Tonal center oder expliziter unknown-Status nötig
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Der gleiche Am-Akkord ist vi in C, i in a.

title: SKILL ist kein Quellenarchiv
assertion_or_proposal: Lange Wissensartikel bleiben in KB, Skill enthält Verfahren
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Kleine dynamisch geladene Referenzen sind zulässig.

title: Progression Event context
assertion_or_proposal: Onset, duration, chord und ggf. analysis_candidates vorhanden
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Auftrag kann nur lose Akkordliste liefern, dann pending timing.

title: Leittonbewegung zur Tonika
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Jazz und Pop können Bewegung anders führen.

title: Sekundärdominante
applicability_conditions: tonal context C; A7 before Dm
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Ohne Dm-Auflösung bleibt alternative Analyse offen.

title: Minor V7
assertion_or_proposal: G# kann Leitton nach A sein
non_applicability_or_counterexample: In Äolisch ist Em ohne G# ebenfalls möglich.

title: Trugschluss
assertion_or_proposal: V7–vi kann klassisch als Trugschluss wirken
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Nicht jedes V→vi in einem Pop-Loop ist klassische Kadenz.

title: Mollsubdominante
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Nicht jedes Fm verlangt Borrowed-Chord-Erzählung.

title: Guide tones in ii-V-I
assertion_or_proposal: F→F→E und C→B→B als mögliche Stimmenbewegungen
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Nicht die einzig mögliche Voicing-Wahl.

title: Tritonussubstitution
assertion_or_proposal: Db7→C als chromatische Alternative bei kompatibler Melodie
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Nicht für jeden Stil/Beat und jede Melodie sinnvoll.

title: Plagaler Rückgang
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Authentische Kadenz ist im klassischen Modell anders definiert.

title: Rhythmische Verdichtung
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Wiederholung bei geringem Tempo kann auch Ruhe erzeugen.

title: Registeröffnung
assertion_or_proposal: Breitere registrale Anlage kann den Höhepunkt unterstützen
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Leises, enges Register kann absichtlich intensiver wirken.

title: Metrische Platzierung
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Nicht jeder Downbeat schließt eine Phrase.

title: Modaler Ruhepunkt

title: Basslinie abwärts

title: Melodieton bei Reharmonisierung

title: Chromatische Medianten
assertion_or_proposal: Gemeinsamer Ton C und kleine Stimmenbewegungen können Verbindung erklären
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Funktionsanalyse ist nicht automatisch ausgeschlossen.

title: Axis zwei Tonalitäten
assertion_or_proposal: vi–IV–I–V in C oder i–bVI–bIII–bVII in A
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Melodie und Form müssen Entscheidung stützen.

title: Blues I7
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Klassisches V7/IV kann in anderem Kontext sinnvoll sein.

title: Plateau Loop
assertion_or_proposal: IV–V–vi als potenziell tonikal ambiguose Schleife
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Nicht jede identische Akkordreihenfolge erzeugt Hybrid-Tonicity.

title: Nichtfunktionale Medianten
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Andere Linsen sind je Kontext möglich.

title: Harmonic Rhythm
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Keine lineare universelle Spannungsmetrik.

title: Cadence requires phrase
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Ohne Metrik, Melodie und Form keine PAC-Zusage.

title: Motividentität

non_applicability_or_counterexample: Originalität und Erkennbarkeit sind nicht mechanisch garantiert.

title: Kompositorischer Kontrast
non_applicability_or_counterexample: Mehr gleichzeitige Änderungen können künstlerisch beabsichtigt sein.

title: Orchestration-Pass

non_applicability_or_counterexample: Instrumentenbereich braucht spezielle validierte Referenz.

title: Voice-Leading-Ranking

non_applicability_or_counterexample: Minimal movement != best music.

title: Quellenauswahl

title: Composing review
